## Getting Started (AngleSharp.Js)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/general/basics/
> Project: AngleSharp.Js (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Js)
> Package: AngleSharp.Js 1.2.3 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Js`
> Docs revision: dfd5fb3a9a4a0412ecd0af5ab760881e2705e4af

AngleSharp.Js runs JavaScript against an AngleSharp document. It integrates the [Jint](https://github.com/sebastienros/jint) interpreter with AngleSharp, so scripts can read and change the same DOM that your .NET code uses. This is useful when processing pages whose behavior depends on script execution, evaluating a snippet in a document context, or hosting JavaScript APIs alongside your application.

### Install and configure

Install the package:

```ps1
Install-Package AngleSharp.Js
```

Add `WithJs()` to the AngleSharp configuration. Add `WithEventLoop()` when scripts, events, or resource callbacks must run in the browser-like task queue. Add a loader when the document needs to fetch external scripts or other resources.

For many real-world scripts, `WithJs()` alone is not enough. AngleSharp.Js exposes interfaces from the AngleSharp services present in the browsing context, so you usually want to include AngleSharp.Io and AngleSharp.Css to provide most of the required API surface.

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions
    {
        IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true,
    })
    .WithCss()
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();

var context = BrowsingContext.New(configuration);
var document = await context.OpenAsync("https://example.com");

await document.WaitUntilAvailable();
```

Some highly specialized scripts may also depend on additional  AngleSharp packages. For example, in niche scenarios, libraries such as AngleSharp.Wasm can be relevant.

`WithJs()` registers the JavaScript scripting service, support for inline event attributes such as `onclick`, a navigation handler for `javascript:` URLs, structured cloning (for `postMessage` and workers) and the host for custom elements. It does not register a loader, an event loop or a navigator; `WithNavigator()` from AngleSharp.Io provides a full `navigator`.

#### Customize the event loop

`WithEventLoop()` creates a dedicated `JsEventLoop` for each browsing context. To select the
stack size of its worker thread, use the factory overload:

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop(_ => new JsEventLoop(32 * 1024 * 1024));
```

You can instead provide an `IEventLoop` implementation when the host application owns
scheduling. Use the factory overload when each browsing context needs an independent loop.

#### Configure the execution stack

`JsScriptingOptions.MaxCallStackDepth` defaults to 10,000. It makes deep JavaScript recursion
fail with a JavaScript error rather than exhausting the process stack. Leave it positive unless
you explicitly accept the risk of an uncatchable `StackOverflowException`.

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .WithJs(new JsScriptingOptions
    {
        MaxCallStackDepth = 5000,
    });
```

#### Keep the source of functions

Like in browsers, `Function.prototype.toString()` gives the source of a function written in a
script, which some pages rely on (e.g. MediaWiki stores the code of its modules this way). This
keeps the source of the scripts in memory as long as their functions live; setting
`JsScriptingOptions.RetainFunctionSourceText` to `false` turns it off, and `toString()` then gives
`function name() { [native code] }`.

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .WithJs(new JsScriptingOptions
    {
        RetainFunctionSourceText = false,
    });
```

#### Configure the Jint engine

Register an `EngineCreator` to construct the Jint engine yourself, for example to limit the statements, time or memory a script may use. The delegate runs once per window and must build the engine from the supplied options:

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .With(new EngineCreator((window, options) => new Jint.Engine(options
        .MaxStatements(1_000_000)
        .TimeoutInterval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)))))
    .WithJs();
```

### Execute JavaScript

HTML `<script>` elements execute while AngleSharp processes the document. For a script you want to run yourself, call `ExecuteScript` on the document. The return value is converted to the corresponding .NET value where possible: numbers become `Double`, DOM objects the AngleSharp objects, `undefined` the string `"undefined"`, and other objects stay Jint values.

```cs
var document = await BrowsingContext.New(Configuration.Default.WithJs())
    .OpenAsync(request => request.Content("<p class=message>Hello</p>"));

var message = (String)document.ExecuteScript(
    "document.querySelector('.message').textContent");
```

`ExecuteScript(scriptCode, scriptType, sourceUrl)` accepts an optional MIME type and source
URL. JavaScript MIME types are evaluated as classic scripts. `module` runs an ES module and
`importmap` loads an import map. Other script types return `undefined`.

Each document window gets its own Jint engine and JavaScript global state. Reusing the same
configuration does not share variables between documents.

#### Wait for queued work

With an event loop configured, use the document extensions to control when work runs:

| API | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `Then(Action<IDocument>)` | Queue .NET work after currently queued script work. |
| `Then(String)` | Queue a JavaScript snippet after currently queued script work. |
| `WhenStable()` | Wait until the work already in the event loop has completed. |
| `WaitUntilAvailable()` | Wait for document completion and then for the event loop to stabilize. |

These methods do not wait for asynchronous I/O that a script starts after the marker has been
queued. For example, await an event dispatched by the script after an `XMLHttpRequest` finishes.

For example, wait for scripts that change the document before reading the result:

```cs
var document = await context.OpenAsync("https://example.com")
    .WaitUntilAvailable();

var title = document.Title;
```

### Connect JavaScript and .NET

#### Provide host values

Create `JsScriptingService` yourself when scripts need application-provided values. Add entries
to `External` before a document first executes JavaScript; these values are copied into every
new document engine.

```cs
var scripting = new JsScriptingService();
scripting.External["getGreeting"] = new Func<String>(() => "Hello from .NET");

var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .With(scripting)
    .WithEventLoop();

var document = await BrowsingContext.New(configuration)
    .OpenAsync(request => request.Content(
        "<script>document.body.textContent = getGreeting()</script>"));
```

JavaScript can call delegates and access the public members of objects exposed this way. For
advanced integration, `GetOrCreateJint(document)` returns the document's Jint `Engine`, which
lets host code inspect JavaScript values or invoke JavaScript functions directly.

Registering a `JsScriptingService` directly does not add the auxiliary integration that
`WithJs()` supplies: inline event-handler attributes and `javascript:` URL navigation.

#### Capture `console.log`

`console.log` forwards its arguments to an `IConsoleLogger` registered for the browsing
context. Provide one with `WithConsoleLogger`:

```cs
var configuration = Configuration.Default
    .WithJs()
    .WithConsoleLogger(_ => new ApplicationConsoleLogger());
```

Implement `IConsoleLogger.Log(Object[] values)` to send the values to your application's
logging system. Without a logger, calls to `console.log` do not produce output.

For example, a minimal logger can forward values to `System.Diagnostics`:

```cs
sealed class ApplicationConsoleLogger : IConsoleLogger
{
    public void Log(Object[] values)
    {
        Debug.WriteLine(String.Join(" ", values));
    }
}
```

### DOM APIs and integration points

AngleSharp.Js exposes AngleSharp DOM interfaces to JavaScript dynamically. The available
surface therefore follows the AngleSharp services registered in the browsing context. For
example, adding CSS support also makes its AngleSharp DOM types available to scripts.

In addition to the DOM provided by AngleSharp, the package supplies:

- `console`, `atob`, `btoa`, `structuredClone`, `queueMicrotask`, `DOMParser`, `Image`, `Audio`, and `screen`.
- `requestAnimationFrame`, `requestIdleCallback`, `performance`, `crypto`, `TextEncoder`, and `TextDecoder`.
- `Worker`, `SharedWorker`, `MessageChannel`, and `window.postMessage`.
- `javascript:` URL navigation.
- Inline event-handler attributes and DOM event callbacks.
- ES modules and import maps through Jint's module loader.

#### Built-in browser facades

The additional browser-like APIs are deliberately small. Use this table when deciding whether
they meet a script's needs:

| API | Available behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `DOMParser` | `parseFromString` creates a document through the configured `IDocumentFactory`. The requested MIME type must be supported by that configuration. |
| `Image` | Creates an AngleSharp `<img>` element; optional width and height become its display dimensions. |
| `window.postMessage` | Queues a `message` event on the current window. It requires an event loop; it does not transfer objects, deliver to another browsing context, or enforce `targetOrigin`. |
| `console` | All methods are available; their arguments (or, for `count`/`time*`, the formatted result) are passed to the `IConsoleLogger`. The severity is not distinguished. |
| `screen` | Exposes fixed 1920-by-1080 dimensions and 24-bit color depth for compatibility. |

APIs such as `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket` and `localStorage` come from AngleSharp.Io, and `getComputedStyle` or `matchMedia` from AngleSharp.Css. They appear once the respective
services are registered (e.g. `WithRequesters()` or `WithCss()`).

The `WithEventLoop` overloads accept either an existing `IEventLoop` or a factory for one.

### Supported behavior and limitations

AngleSharp.Js is a DOM and scripting integration, not a browser runtime. Script behavior
depends on the installed Jint and AngleSharp versions, plus the services that your
configuration supplies. Test the browser APIs your application relies on instead of assuming
complete browser parity.

Notable limitations include:

- The package does not calculate layout. Its `scroll*`, `client*`, and `offset*` element properties return `0`.
- Without AngleSharp.Io's `WithNavigator()`, `navigator` is minimal (e.g. an empty `userAgent`).
- Network-backed features such as external scripts, modules, workers, `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` require suitable AngleSharp requesters and resource loading configuration.
- The JavaScript engine executes application-provided or page-provided code in your process. Treat untrusted scripts as untrusted code and apply the constraints appropriate to your application.

### Where to go next

- [API Documentation](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/api/index.html.md) lists every public type and how .NET types map to JavaScript.
- [Examples](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/examples/index.html.md) has ready-to-use recipes.
- [Frequently Asked Questions](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/questions/index.html.md) covers common pitfalls.


---

## API Documentation (AngleSharp.Js)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/api/
> Project: AngleSharp.Js (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Js)
> Package: AngleSharp.Js 1.2.3 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Js`
> Docs revision: dfd5fb3a9a4a0412ecd0af5ab760881e2705e4af

This page lists the public .NET API of AngleSharp.Js and explains how .NET types become JavaScript objects. For a guided introduction see [Getting Started](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/general/basics/index.html.md).

The package targets `netstandard2.0`, `net462`, `net472`, `net8.0` and `net10.0`, and depends only on AngleSharp and [Jint](https://github.com/sebastienros/jint).

### Overview

| Type / member | Namespace | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `WithJs()`, `WithJs(JsScriptingOptions)` | `AngleSharp` | Registers the JavaScript engine and its auxiliary services. |
| `WithEventLoop()` and overloads | `AngleSharp` | Registers the event loop that runs scripts, timers and callbacks. |
| `WithConsoleLogger(Func<IBrowsingContext, IConsoleLogger>)` | `AngleSharp` | Routes `console.*` output to your code. |
| `ExecuteScript(document, code, type, sourceUrl)` | `AngleSharp.Js` | Runs JavaScript in the document's engine and returns the result. |
| `Then`, `WhenStable`, `WaitUntilAvailable` | `AngleSharp.Dom` | Synchronize .NET code with the event loop. |
| `JsScriptingService` | `AngleSharp.Scripting` | The `IScriptingService`; holds host values and gives access to the Jint  engine. |
| `JsScriptingOptions` | `AngleSharp.Js` | Call stack depth and function source retention. |
| `EngineCreator` | `AngleSharp.Js` | Delegate service to build the Jint `Engine` yourself (limits, timeouts). |
| `JsEventLoop` | `AngleSharp.Js` | The default `IEventLoop`, a dedicated background thread. |
| `IConsoleLogger` | `AngleSharp.Js` | Receives the values passed to `console.*`. |
| `JsNavigationHandler` | `AngleSharp.Js` | Handles `javascript:` URLs. |
| `DomConstructorFunctionAttribute` | `AngleSharp.Js.Attributes` | Marks a method as a factory-style constructor function (like `Image`). |

Typical `using` directives:

```cs
using AngleSharp;
using AngleSharp.Dom;
using AngleSharp.Js;
using AngleSharp.Scripting; // only for JsScriptingService
```

### Configuration extensions

All of these extend `IConfiguration` and live in `AngleSharp.JsConfigurationExtensions`.

#### `WithJs()` / `WithJs(JsScriptingOptions options)`

Registers:

- a `JsScriptingService` (the engine) configured with a copy of `options`,
- an `EventAttributeObserver`, which turns `onclick="…"` and similar attributes into handlers,
- a `JsNavigationHandler` for `javascript:` URLs,
- a structured clone service (used by `postMessage`, `structuredClone`, workers),
- a custom element host, so `customElements.define` works with JavaScript classes.

Calling `WithJs` does **not** register an event loop or a loader. Most documents that run scripts need both (see `WithEventLoop` and AngleSharp's `WithDefaultLoader`).

#### `WithEventLoop()`

```cs
IConfiguration WithEventLoop(this IConfiguration configuration);
IConfiguration WithEventLoop(this IConfiguration configuration, IEventLoop loop);
IConfiguration WithEventLoop(this IConfiguration configuration, Func<IBrowsingContext, IEventLoop> creator);
```

The parameterless overload creates one `JsEventLoop` per browsing context. Pass an instance to share one loop, or a factory to customize the loop per context. Each overload replaces a previously registered `IEventLoop` (`WithOnly`).

Without an event loop, scripts still run, but nothing is queued: timers, `postMessage` to the window, and the `Then`/`WhenStable` synchronization have nothing to wait for.

#### `WithConsoleLogger(Func<IBrowsingContext, IConsoleLogger> createLogger)`

Registers a factory for an `IConsoleLogger`. It is ignored if a logger is already registered.

### Running scripts from .NET

#### `ExecuteScript`

```cs
public static Object ExecuteScript(this IDocument document, String scriptCode,
    String scriptType = null, String sourceUrl = null);
```

Defined in `AngleSharp.Js.JsApiExtensions`. Runs `scriptCode` synchronously in the engine of the document's window and returns the completion value of the script (the value of the last expression statement), converted to .NET:

| JavaScript value | .NET value |
| --- | --- |
| `undefined` (also a script ending in a declaration such as `var x = 1;`) | the **string** `"undefined"` |
| `null` | `null` |
| boolean | `Boolean` |
| number | `Double` (always, also for integers) |
| string | `String` |
| BigInt | `System.Numerics.BigInteger` |
| DOM object (`document.body`, …) | the AngleSharp object (`IHtmlElement`, …) |
| other objects, arrays, dates, functions | the Jint object (`Jint.Native.JsObject`, `JsArray`, `JsDate`, function), a `JsValue` |

When you need structured data, return `JSON.stringify(…)` and deserialize it in .NET.

Remarks:

- `scriptType` defaults to `text/javascript`. Any JavaScript MIME type runs a classic script, `module` runs an ES module, `importmap` registers an import map; other types return `null`.
- `sourceUrl` is used in error messages and stack traces, and as the base address for imports.
- Errors are thrown to the caller: a JavaScript error as `Jint.Runtime.JavaScriptException` (also for syntax errors), a violated Jint constraint as the respective Jint exception (e.g. `StatementsCountOverflowException`).
- It returns `null` when the configuration has no `JsScriptingService` or the document is in a sandboxed frame that may not run scripts.
- It does **not** go through the event loop. If page scripts are still loading, wait for them first (`WaitUntilAvailable`), or queue the call with `Then(String)`.

#### Synchronizing with the event loop

Defined in `AngleSharp.Dom.JsDocumentExtensions`; every method exists for `IDocument` and for `Task<IDocument>`, so they can be chained directly after `OpenAsync`.

| Method | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Then(Action<IDocument> action)` | Queues `action` on the event loop and completes after it ran. Runs immediately if there is no event loop. |
| `Then(String jsSource)` | Same, but runs JavaScript via `ExecuteScript`. |
| `WhenStable()` | Completes once every task queued so far has run. |
| `WaitUntilAvailable(CancellationToken cancellation = default)` | Waits for the `load` event of the document (if not yet complete), then for `WhenStable()`. The token aborts the wait for `load`. |

```cs
var document = await context.OpenAsync(address)
    .WaitUntilAvailable()
    .Then("document.title = 'changed'");
```

The returned tasks only cover work already in the queue. Work started later, for example a `setTimeout` callback or an `XMLHttpRequest` response, is not awaited; see the [FAQ](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/questions/index.html.md#how-do-i-wait-for-a-timer-or-a-request-started-by-a-script).

### `JsScriptingService`

Namespace `AngleSharp.Scripting`. `WithJs()` creates one for you; create it yourself when you want to use `External` or `GetOrCreateJint`, and register it with `.With(service)`.

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `JsScriptingService()` / `JsScriptingService(JsScriptingOptions options)` | Creates the service. The options are copied. |
| `IDictionary<String, Object> External` | Values set as globals in every engine created afterwards (one engine per window). |
| `Engine GetOrCreateJint(IDocument document)` | The Jint engine of the document's window, created on first use. |
| `Object EvaluateScript(IDocument document, String source, String type, String sourceUrl)` | What `ExecuteScript` calls. |
| `String Type` | `text/javascript`. |

To keep the inline-event and `javascript:` URL support, register the service *and* call `WithJs()`, or prefer the `EngineCreator` service for host globals:

```cs
var scripting = new JsScriptingService();
scripting.External["appName"] = "MyApp";

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(scripting)
    .WithEventLoop();
```

Each window has its own engine: `GetOrCreateJint(frameDocument)` returns a different engine than for the top-level document, and global variables are not shared between documents.

The page's scripts run in a window scope layered over the Jint global. `engine.Evaluate`, `engine.Execute`, `engine.GetValue("name")` and `engine.Invoke("name", …)` do not see the variables and functions the page declared. Use `ExecuteScript` to run code or to obtain a function, and `engine.Invoke(JsValue function, params Object[] arguments)` to call it.

### `JsScriptingOptions`

Namespace `AngleSharp.Js`. Copied when the service is created.

| Property | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Int32 MaxCallStackDepth` | `10000` | Recursion depth before the script gets a `RangeError` ("Maximum call stack size exceeded"). Zero or less removes the guard; deep recursion then crashes the process with a `StackOverflowException`. |
| `Boolean RetainFunctionSourceText` | `true` | Keeps the source text so `Function.prototype.toString()` returns it. Turn off to save memory; functions then print as `function name() { [native code] }`. |

### `EngineCreator`

```cs
public delegate Jint.Engine EngineCreator(IWindow window, Jint.Options options);
```

Register an `EngineCreator` (or a `Func<IBrowsingContext, EngineCreator>`) as a service to create the Jint engine yourself. It is called once per window, before any page script runs.

- Always construct the engine with the given `options`: they carry the DOM object wrapper, the module loader and the call stack guard. Add to them, do not replace them.
- Return a new `Engine` each time; returning `null` throws `InvalidOperationException`.
- The DOM is installed after the delegate returns, so do not touch DOM objects in it. Setting host globals with `engine.SetValue` is fine.
- Workers created by the page also use the creator.

```cs
using Jint;

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(new EngineCreator((window, options) => new Engine(options
        .MaxStatements(1_000_000)
        .TimeoutInterval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5))
        .LimitMemory(64 * 1024 * 1024)
        .RegexTimeoutInterval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1)))))
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();
```

An inline page script violating a constraint is reported to the browsing context (see [error handling](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/examples/index.html.md#collect-script-errors)); `ExecuteScript` throws the Jint exception.

### `JsEventLoop`

Namespace `AngleSharp.Js`, implements `IEventLoop` and `IDisposable`.

| Constructor | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `JsEventLoop()` | Loop with the default worker thread stack size. |
| `JsEventLoop(IBrowsingContext context)` | Same, used by `WithEventLoop()`. |
| `JsEventLoop(Int32 maxStackSize)` | Uses the given stack size (bytes) for the worker thread. Raise it together with `MaxCallStackDepth`. |

All tasks of the loop run on one dedicated thread, one after another, ordered by priority (scripts are queued as critical). After each task the pending promise jobs (microtasks) run. Exceptions thrown by a task are reported as `error` events of the browsing context.

### `IConsoleLogger`

```cs
public interface IConsoleLogger
{
    void Log(Object[] values);
}
```

Every `console` method ends up in `Log`. The values are the converted arguments (strings, numbers, AngleSharp objects, …).

| Script call | What `Log` receives |
| --- | --- |
| `log`, `info`, `warn`, `error`, `debug`, `trace`, `dir`, `dirxml`, `table` | the arguments |
| `assert(condition, …)` | the arguments after `condition`, only if `condition` is falsy |
| `group(…)`, `groupCollapsed(…)` | the arguments, if any |
| `count(label)` | `"label: n"` |
| `time(label)` / `timeLog(label, …)` / `timeEnd(label)` | the elapsed time in milliseconds |
| `groupEnd()`, `clear()`, `countReset()` | nothing |

The severity is not passed on: `console.error` and `console.log` look the same to the logger.

### `JsNavigationHandler`

Registered by `WithJs()`. Navigating to a `javascript:` URL (e.g. clicking `<a href="javascript:doSomething()">`) runs the code in the current document instead of loading a new one.

### `DomConstructorFunctionAttribute`

Namespace `AngleSharp.Js.Attributes`. Placed on a static extension method of `IWindow` to expose it as a constructor function under the given name, the way `Image(width, height)` and `Audio(src)` are built:

```cs
[DomConstructorFunction("Image")]
public static IHtmlImageElement Image(this IWindow window, Int32? width = null, Int32? height = null)
```

### How .NET types become JavaScript

There is no generated binding code. When an engine is created, AngleSharp.Js reflects over the exported types of every assembly whose name starts with `AngleSharp` and that provides a service registered in the browsing context (AngleSharp itself, AngleSharp.Js, AngleSharp.Css, AngleSharp.Io, …). The attributes from `AngleSharp.Attributes` drive what scripts see:

| Attribute | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `[DomName("X")]` on an interface or class | The JavaScript interface name (`HTMLDivElement`). Its instances get `X.prototype`. |
| `[DomName("x")]` on a member | Exposes the property, method or event under that name. Methods of the same name are overloads. |
| `[DomConstructor]` on a constructor | `new X(…)` is possible from script. |
| `[DomExposed("Window")]` on a type | Publishes the interface on the window (or on another interface or namespace, e.g. `[DomExposed("Worker")]`). On a static class, its `[DomName]` extension methods are added to the type they extend. |
| `[DomNoInterfaceObject]` | Members are available, but no global constructor is published. |
| `[DomInitDict]` on a parameter | The parameter is filled from the members of an options object. |
| `[DomLiterals]` on an enum | The enum values are strings (`"loading"`), otherwise numbers. |
| `[DomPutForwards("x")]` | Assigning the property assigns its member `x` (e.g. `location = "…"`). |

Value conversions follow WebIDL:

- **Into .NET:** JS numbers to any numeric type; functions to delegates (also bound functions and callable proxies); objects with `handleEvent`/`acceptNode` to the respective listener or filter; any iterable to arrays and the generic interfaces arrays implement; BufferSources to `Byte[]` when the parameter is `Object`; promises to `Task`; BigInt to `BigInteger`.
- **Out of .NET:** `[DomLiterals]` enums to strings, other enums to numbers (the enum type is exposed as an object of constants); `Byte[]` to a new `ArrayBuffer`; `ArraySegment<Byte>` to a new  `Uint8Array`; `Memory<Byte>` to an `ArrayBuffer` sharing the memory; other arrays to JS arrays; `IDictionary<String, Object>` to a plain object; `Task` to a promise; `DateTime` to `Date`; delegates to functions; DOM exceptions to errors of their own class (`instanceof Error`).
- Identity is preserved: the same AngleSharp node is always the same JavaScript object, so `document.body === document.body` holds and expandos stay attached.
- Members live on the prototype of the interface declaring them and are writable, so polyfills can patch them (`Element.prototype.querySelector = …`).


---

## Examples (AngleSharp.Js)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/examples/
> Project: AngleSharp.Js (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Js)
> Package: AngleSharp.Js 1.2.3 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Js`
> Docs revision: dfd5fb3a9a4a0412ecd0af5ab760881e2705e4af

This is a (growing) list of examples for every-day usage of AngleSharp.Js. All examples assume these `using` directives:

```cs
using AngleSharp;
using AngleSharp.Dom;
using AngleSharp.Js;
```

### Evaluate an expression against HTML

No event loop or loader is needed when you only want to run your own code against a document. The value of the last expression is returned.

```cs
var context = BrowsingContext.New(Configuration.Default.WithJs());
var document = await context.OpenAsync(req => req.Content(@"
    <ul>
      <li>One</li>
      <li>Two</li>
      <li>Three</li>
    </ul>"));

var count = (Double)document.ExecuteScript("document.querySelectorAll('li').length");
var text = (String)document.ExecuteScript(
    "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('li'), li => li.textContent).join(', ')");
// count == 3, text == "One, Two, Three"
```

Numbers always come back as `Double`, `undefined` as the string `"undefined"`, and DOM objects as the AngleSharp objects (an `IElement`, …). Return a string (e.g. via `JSON.stringify`) when you need a structured result:

```cs
var json = (String)document.ExecuteScript(
    "JSON.stringify([...document.querySelectorAll('li')].map(li => ({ text: li.textContent })))");
```

### Load a page and read the DOM after its scripts ran

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default
    .WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions { IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true })
    .WithCss()
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();

var context = BrowsingContext.New(config);
var document = await context.OpenAsync("https://example.com")
    .WaitUntilAvailable();

Console.WriteLine(document.Title);
Console.WriteLine(document.Body.InnerHtml);
```

`IsResourceLoadingEnabled` is what makes AngleSharp download `<script src="…">`. Without it only inline scripts run.

### Run scripts on a document built from a string

Scripts in the source run while the document is parsed. Use `WaitUntilAvailable` before reading the result, because the event loop runs them on its own thread.

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default.WithJs().WithEventLoop();
var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenAsync(req => req.Content(@"
    <div id=out></div>
    <script>
      document.getElementById('out').textContent = [1, 2, 3].map(x => x * 2).join();
    </script>"))
    .WaitUntilAvailable();

var output = document.GetElementById("out").TextContent; // "2,4,6"
```

### Interact with the page: click, then inspect

Events dispatched from .NET reach JavaScript listeners, and the other way round.

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default.WithJs().WithEventLoop();
var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenAsync(req => req.Content(@"
    <button id=btn>Count</button><span id=n>0</span>
    <script>
      let n = 0;
      document.getElementById('btn').addEventListener('click', () => {
        document.getElementById('n').textContent = ++n;
      });
    </script>"))
    .WaitUntilAvailable();

var button = (IHtmlElement)document.GetElementById("btn"); // AngleSharp.Html.Dom
button.DoClick();
button.DoClick();

await document.WhenStable();
var clicks = document.GetElementById("n").TextContent; // "2"
```

Inline handlers such as `<button onclick="…">` work as well, as long as the configuration uses `WithJs()`.

### Queue work after the page's scripts

`Then` runs .NET code or JavaScript on the event loop, after everything queued so far:

```cs
var document = await context.OpenAsync(address)
    .WaitUntilAvailable()
    .Then("window.scrollTo(0, 0); document.title += ' (processed)'")
    .Then(doc => Console.WriteLine(doc.Title));
```

### Wait for something a script does later

`WhenStable` and `WaitUntilAvailable` do not wait for timers or network requests started by a script. Wait for an observable effect instead; with a `TaskCompletionSource` and a host function:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Scripting;

var ready = new TaskCompletionSource<String>();
var scripting = new JsScriptingService();
scripting.External["notifyHost"] = new Action<String>(value => ready.TrySetResult(value));

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(scripting)
    .WithEventLoop();

var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenAsync(req => req.Content(@"
    <script>
      setTimeout(() => notifyHost('done after timer'), 50);
    </script>"));

var result = await ready.Task.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)); // .NET 6+
```

Alternatively, poll for a selector until a timeout:

```cs
static async Task<IElement> WaitForSelectorAsync(IDocument document, String selector, TimeSpan timeout)
{
    var end = DateTime.UtcNow + timeout;

    while (DateTime.UtcNow < end)
    {
        await document.WhenStable();
        var element = document.QuerySelector(selector);

        if (element != null)
        {
            return element;
        }

        await Task.Delay(25);
    }

    return null;
}
```

### Expose .NET functions and objects to scripts

Values in `JsScriptingService.External` become globals of every document. Delegates become functions, other objects are exposed with their public members (Jint also accepts camel-cased names, so `calc.Add` and `calc.add` both work).

```cs
using AngleSharp.Scripting;

public sealed class Calculator
{
    public Int32 Add(Int32 a, Int32 b) => a + b;
}

var scripting = new JsScriptingService();
scripting.External["calc"] = new Calculator();
scripting.External["log"] = new Action<String>(message => Console.WriteLine(message));

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(scripting)
    .WithJs()   // keeps inline event attributes and javascript: URLs working
    .WithEventLoop();

var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenNewAsync();
var sum = document.ExecuteScript("calc.add(2, 3)"); // 5.0
```

The same can be done per engine in an `EngineCreator`, which also lets you set Jint options:

```cs
using Jint;

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(new EngineCreator((window, options) =>
    {
        var engine = new Engine(options);
        engine.SetValue("hostVersion", "1.0");
        return engine;
    }))
    .WithJs();
```

### Call a JavaScript function from .NET

For simple cases build the call as source:

```cs
var greeting = (String)document.ExecuteScript("greet('World')");
```

To pass .NET values without string concatenation, read the function with `ExecuteScript` and invoke it on the document's Jint engine:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Scripting;
using Jint.Native;

var scripting = new JsScriptingService();
var config = Configuration.Default.With(scripting).WithJs().WithEventLoop();
var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenAsync(req => req.Content(
    "<script>function greet(name) { return 'Hello ' + name; }</script>"))
    .WaitUntilAvailable();

var engine = scripting.GetOrCreateJint(document);
var greet = (JsValue)document.ExecuteScript("greet");
var greeting = engine.Invoke(greet, "World").AsString(); // "Hello World"
```

Do not use `engine.Evaluate(…)`, `engine.Execute(…)` or `engine.Invoke("greet", …)` for this: they bypass the window scope the page's scripts run in, so the page's globals are not found ("greet is not defined"). Always go through `ExecuteScript`.

### Limit untrusted or runaway scripts

```cs
using Jint;

var config = Configuration.Default
    .With(new EngineCreator((window, options) => new Engine(options
        .MaxStatements(1_000_000)
        .TimeoutInterval(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2))
        .LimitMemory(32 * 1024 * 1024))))
    .WithJs(new JsScriptingOptions { MaxCallStackDepth = 2000 })
    .WithEventLoop();
```

`ExecuteScript` throws the corresponding Jint exception (e.g. `StatementsCountOverflowException`, `TimeoutException`, `MemoryLimitExceededException`) or a `JavaScriptException` for "Maximum call stack size exceeded". Page scripts that hit a limit stop and report the error to the browsing context (next example). Note that the limits apply per script run, not to the whole page lifetime.

### Collect script errors

Uncaught errors of page scripts, timers and event listeners do not throw into your code; they are dispatched as `error` events of the browsing context (after the page's own `window.onerror`).

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser.Dom.Events; // TrackEvent

var errors = new List<Exception>();
var context = BrowsingContext.New(Configuration.Default.WithJs().WithEventLoop());
context.AddEventListener("error", (sender, ev) =>
{
    if (ev is TrackEvent track)
    {
        errors.Add(track.Error); // usually a Jint.Runtime.JavaScriptException
    }
});

var document = await context.OpenAsync(req => req.Content(
    "<script>undefinedFunction()</script>"))
    .WaitUntilAvailable();
// errors[0].Message == "undefinedFunction is not defined"
```

Errors of `ExecuteScript` are thrown directly:

```cs
try
{
    document.ExecuteScript("JSON.parse('{')");
}
catch (Jint.Runtime.JavaScriptException ex)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{ex.Message} at {ex.Location.Start.Line}:{ex.Location.Start.Column}");
}
```

### Forward `console` output

```cs
public sealed class ConsoleForwarder : IConsoleLogger
{
    public void Log(Object[] values) =>
        System.Console.WriteLine("[js] " + String.Join(" ", values));
}

var config = Configuration.Default
    .WithJs()
    .WithConsoleLogger(_ => new ConsoleForwarder());
```

All `console` methods (`log`, `warn`, `error`, `info`, `debug`, `count`, `time`, …) arrive here. Use one logger per context (the factory receives the `IBrowsingContext`) when you need to tell the pages apart. Note that `System.Console` must be fully qualified inside code that also imports `AngleSharp.Js.Dom`, which has a `Console` class.

### ES modules and import maps

Module scripts are fetched through the configured loader, so give the context a requester for the addresses involved:

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default
    .WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions { IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true })
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();

var document = await BrowsingContext.New(config).OpenAsync(req => req
    .Address("https://example.com/app/")
    .Content(@"
        <script type=importmap>
          { ""imports"": { ""lodash/"": ""https://cdn.example.com/lodash-es/"" } }
        </script>
        <script type=module>
          import chunk from 'lodash/chunk.js';
          document.body.dataset.chunks = JSON.stringify(chunk([1, 2, 3, 4], 2));
        </script>"))
    .WaitUntilAvailable();
```

From .NET a module can also be run directly; relative imports resolve against `sourceUrl`:

```cs
document.ExecuteScript("import { x } from './lib.js'; globalThis.result = x;",
    "module", "https://example.com/app/main.js");
```

Modules support top-level `await`, dynamic `import()`, `import.meta.url`/`import.meta.resolve()`, JSON modules and CSS module scripts (`import sheet from './a.css' with { type: 'css' }`, needs `WithCss()`).

### Workers and message channels

`Worker`, `SharedWorker` and `MessageChannel` are available to scripts. Worker scripts are loaded through the loader, so resource loading must be enabled:

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default
    .WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions { IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true })
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();
```

```js
const worker = new Worker('worker.js');
worker.onmessage = e => document.title = e.data;
worker.postMessage({ numbers: [1, 2, 3] });
```

Messages are copied with the structured clone algorithm;  `MessagePort`s can be transferred.

### Use a different engine per page or per context

Register a factory to get a fresh `EngineCreator` (and thus separate host state) per browsing context:

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default
    .With<EngineCreator>(context => (window, options) => new Engine(options.MaxStatements(10_000)))
    .WithJs()
    .WithEventLoop();
```


---

## Questions (AngleSharp.Js)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/questions/
> Project: AngleSharp.Js (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Js)
> Package: AngleSharp.Js 1.2.3 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Js`
> Docs revision: dfd5fb3a9a4a0412ecd0af5ab760881e2705e4af

### Why do the scripts of my page not run?

Check these, in order:

1. `WithJs()` is part of the configuration.
2. External scripts (`<script src="…">`) need a loader **with resource loading enabled**: `WithDefaultLoader(new LoaderOptions { IsResourceLoadingEnabled = true })`.
3. You read the DOM too early. Scripts run on the event loop thread; `await` the document with `WaitUntilAvailable()` before reading it.
4. The script has an error. Errors are not thrown to you; listen for `error` on the browsing context (see [Collect script errors](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/examples/index.html.md#collect-script-errors)).
5. The page is inside a sandboxed `<iframe>` without `allow-scripts`, which never runs scripts.

### Why is `fetch` / `XMLHttpRequest` / `localStorage` / `getComputedStyle` undefined?

The JavaScript surface is derived from the AngleSharp services registered in the browsing context. AngleSharp.Js itself contributes only its own APIs (see below). Many common browser APIs live in other packages:

| Script API | Comes from | Register with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `WebSocket`, `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, cookies | AngleSharp.Io | `WithRequesters()` or `WithIo(new IoOptions())`, plus `WithDefaultLoader()` |
| `navigator.userAgent` and other navigator details | AngleSharp.Io | `WithNavigator()` |
| `getComputedStyle`, `matchMedia`, `CSSStyleSheet`, `element.style`, `CSS.*` | AngleSharp.Css | `WithCss()` |
| DOM, events, timers, `URL`, `Blob`, `MutationObserver`, `customElements` | AngleSharp | always |

If an API is missing, test with `typeof X` in `ExecuteScript` after adding the package that implements it.

### Which APIs does AngleSharp.Js add itself?

On top of what the registered AngleSharp libraries expose:

- `console` (all methods, forwarded to an `IConsoleLogger`)
- `atob`, `btoa`, `structuredClone`, `queueMicrotask`
- `requestAnimationFrame` / `cancelAnimationFrame`, `requestIdleCallback` / `cancelIdleCallback`
- `postMessage` on the window, `MessageChannel`, `MessagePort`
- `Worker`, `SharedWorker`
- `performance` (`now`, `mark`, `measure`, entries) and `PerformanceObserver`
- `crypto.getRandomValues`, `crypto.randomUUID`, and `crypto.subtle` (not on .NET Framework)
- `TextEncoder`, `TextDecoder`
- `DOMParser`, `Image`, `Audio`, `screen`, `DOMException`
- `window.origin`, `isSecureContext`, `parent`, `top`, `length`, `window.event`
- ES modules, import maps, JSON and CSS module scripts
- inline event attributes (`onclick="…"`) and `javascript:` URLs

The JavaScript language itself (ES2015–ES2025: classes, `async`/`await`, `Proxy`, `BigInt`, iterator helpers, …) is provided by Jint.

### Why are `offsetWidth`, `clientHeight`, `scrollTop` and friends zero?

AngleSharp does not lay out or render pages. The `offset*`, `client*` and `scroll*` properties exist so that scripts do not fail, but always return `0`. Scripts that make decisions based on sizes or visibility may therefore take a different path than in a browser. If you need layout, AngleSharp.Css's render tree gives an approximation, but it is not fed back into these properties.

### Why does `ExecuteScript` return `"undefined"` instead of `null`?

`undefined` is converted to the string `"undefined"`. A script whose last statement is a declaration (`var x = 1;`, `function f() {}`) has no completion value and therefore also returns it. End the script with an expression (`x`) to get a value. Numbers are always `Double`; objects and arrays come back as Jint values, so return `JSON.stringify(…)` when you want plain data.

### Why does `engine.Evaluate(…)` not see the page's functions?

The page's scripts run in a scope bound to the window, not directly on the Jint global object. `Engine.Evaluate`, `Execute`, `GetValue` and `Invoke(String, …)` work on the bare global and report `X is not defined`. Use `document.ExecuteScript(…)`; to call a function with .NET arguments, obtain it via `ExecuteScript("fnName")` and call `engine.Invoke(function, args)`.

### `WaitUntilAvailable()` returned, but the content is still not there

`WaitUntilAvailable` waits for the `load` event and for the tasks queued at that point. Content that a page produces later — after a `setTimeout`, an `XMLHttpRequest`/`fetch` response, or a promise chain waiting on the network — is not covered. Wait for the effect instead: poll for a selector with a timeout, or expose a callback through `JsScriptingService.External` that the page (or a script you inject with `ExecuteScript`) calls. See [Wait for something a script does later](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/examples/index.html.md#wait-for-something-a-script-does-later).

### How do I wait for a timer or a request started by a script?

Same answer as above: there is no global "network idle" signal. Typical approaches are:

- `await document.WhenStable()` in a loop with `Task.Delay`, until a selector appears;
- inject a hook: `document.ExecuteScript("someLib.on('ready', () => notifyHost())")` with `notifyHost` registered in `External`;
- listen to a DOM event from .NET: `document.AddEventListener("my-event", …)`.

### Can I expose my own .NET classes as real DOM interfaces?

Two ways:

- **Host values (simplest).** Put objects or delegates into `JsScriptingService.External`, or call `engine.SetValue` in an `EngineCreator`. Scripts then use them through Jint's regular CLR interop (public members, also camel-cased).
- **DOM-style bindings.** Decorate the types with `[DomName]`, `[DomExposed("Window")]`, `[DomConstructor]` and friends, exactly like AngleSharp does. These get prototypes, `instanceof`, WebIDL-like conversions and so on. AngleSharp.Js only reflects over assemblies  whose name starts with `AngleSharp` **and** that contribute a service registered in the browsing context (e.g. `.WithOnly<MyService>(_ => new MyService())`). Types in an assembly with another name are not picked up, so use the host values approach for application code.

See [How .NET types become JavaScript](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/js/tutorials/api/index.html.md#how-net-types-become-javascript) for the attribute reference.

### Are global variables shared between documents, frames or contexts?

No. Each window has its own Jint engine with its own globals. Frames get their own window and engine as well; same-origin frames can reach each other through `parent`, `top`, `frames` and `contentWindow` like in a browser, and cross-origin windows only expose the cross-origin-safe members (`postMessage`, `location`, `closed`, …).

### Is it safe to run untrusted scripts?

Scripts run in-process and can call everything that is exposed to them, including the values you put into `External` and whatever the registered AngleSharp services can do (e.g. network access via the loader). There is no isolation like in a browser sandbox. At minimum:

- set limits via an `EngineCreator` (`MaxStatements`, `TimeoutInterval`, `LimitMemory`, `RegexTimeoutInterval`) and keep `MaxCallStackDepth` positive;
- only register the services (loaders, requesters, storage) the script is allowed to use;
- do not expose sensitive .NET objects through `External`;
- consider running untrusted work in a separate process.

### Why is my process crashing with a `StackOverflowException`?

Either `JsScriptingOptions.MaxCallStackDepth` was set to zero or less, or the configured depth needs more native stack than the event loop thread has. Lower `MaxCallStackDepth`, or raise the thread's stack with `WithEventLoop(_ => new JsEventLoop(64 * 1024 * 1024))`.

### Does it work with jQuery, React, Bootstrap, …?

Yes, the test suite runs jQuery 1–4, React 16 and Bootstrap 5 against the DOM. Larger frameworks usually work as long as they do not depend on layout (sizes are always `0`) or on APIs from packages you have not registered. Remember that Jint is an interpreter: a big bundle can take noticeably longer than in a browser. Parsed scripts are cached process-wide, so loading the same library again is cheaper.

### Is it fast?

Jint interprets JavaScript, so CPU-heavy scripts are much slower than in a JIT-compiling browser engine. The DOM binding itself is built lazily and cached, so the per-document overhead is mostly proportional to what the scripts actually touch. Practical tips:

- reuse one `IConfiguration` (and `BrowsingContext` where suitable);
- leave `IsResourceLoadingEnabled` off when you only need inline scripts;
- do not register services whose APIs the scripts do not need;
- set `RetainFunctionSourceText = false` if no script relies on `Function.prototype.toString()`.

### Is `ExecuteScript` thread-safe?

The engine of a window is locked while a script runs, so calls from different threads are serialized. They do not, however, wait for the event loop: if page scripts are still being queued, prefer `document.Then("…")`, which runs your code in order with the page's own tasks.

### Which .NET versions are supported?

The package targets `netstandard2.0`, `net462`, `net472`, `net8.0` and `net10.0`. The Web Cryptography API (`crypto.subtle`) is not available on .NET Framework; `crypto.getRandomValues` and `crypto.randomUUID` are.


---

## Getting Started (AngleSharp.Xml)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/xml/general/basics/
> Project: AngleSharp.Xml (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Xml)
> Package: AngleSharp.Xml 1.3.1 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Xml`
> Docs revision: 1942246134ae20a06d89a996f0bd9f1eaa2fd329

### Requirements

AngleSharp.Xml comes currently in two flavors: on Windows for .NET 4.6 and in general targetting .NET Standard 2.0 platforms.

Most of the features of the library do not require .NET 4.6, which means you could create your own fork and modify it to work with previous versions of the .NET-Framework.

You need to have AngleSharp installed already. This could be done via NuGet:

```ps1
Install-Package AngleSharp
```

### Getting AngleSharp.Xml over NuGet

The simplest way of integrating AngleSharp.Xml to your project is by using NuGet. You can install AngleSharp.Xml by opening the package manager console (PM) and typing in the following statement:

```ps1
Install-Package AngleSharp.Xml
```

You can also use the graphical library package manager ("Manage NuGet Packages for Solution"). Searching for "AngleSharp.Xml" in the official NuGet online feed will find this library.

### Setting up AngleSharp.Xml

To use AngleSharp.Xml you need to add it to your `Configuration` coming from AngleSharp itself.

If you just want a configuration *that works* you should use the following code:

```cs
var config = Configuration.Default
    .WithXml(); // from AngleSharp.Xml
```

This will register a parser for XML related content.
