## Getting Started (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/basics/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

### Packages

The functionality is distributed in two NuGet packages:

| Package | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `AngleSharp.Browser` | The UI-agnostic `BrowserEngine`: navigation, painting, input, profiles, and diagnostics. |
| `AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia` | The `BrowserView` control displaying an engine in an Avalonia application. |

Both target .NET 10. They bring AngleSharp, AngleSharp.Css, AngleSharp.Js, AngleSharp.Io, AngleSharp.Xml, AngleSharp.Wasm and AngleSharp.Renderer along, so no other AngleSharp package has to be installed.

### Getting AngleSharp.Browser over NuGet

For headless use, or to integrate another UI framework, install the engine:

```sh
dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser
```

For an Avalonia application, install the control, which references the engine:

```sh
dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia
```

### Showing a Page in Avalonia

Set the address, and the control does the rest:

```xml
<Window xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
        xmlns:browser="using:AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia">
    <browser:BrowserView Source="https://example.org" />
</Window>
```

The [Avalonia Control](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/avalonia/index.html.md) page has all the details.

### Using the Engine Without a UI

The engine needs nothing but a viewport size:

```cs
using System.IO;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions
{
    ViewportWidth = 1280,
    ViewportHeight = 800,
});

await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

var image = await engine.PaintAsync();
await File.WriteAllBytesAsync("page.png", image!.Data);
```

### First Practical Workflows

#### 1. Read something from the page

AngleSharp is not thread-safe. Code touching the DOM therefore runs on the engine's event loop by using `InvokeAsync`:

```cs
await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

var text = await engine.InvokeAsync(document => document?.QuerySelector("p")?.TextContent);
Console.WriteLine(text);
```

#### 2. Run some JavaScript

`EvaluateScriptAsync` works like the console of a browser's developer tools and returns the completion value converted to .NET:

```cs
var result = await engine.EvaluateScriptAsync("1 + 2");
Console.WriteLine(result);
```

#### 3. Interact like a user

Input is given in CSS pixels relative to the viewport. Everything a real click does happens, including following links and focusing text fields:

```cs
await engine.ClickAsync(40, 390);
await engine.TextInputAsync("Hello");
await engine.KeyDownAsync("Enter");
```

#### 4. Load your own markup

Pages do not have to come from the network:

```cs
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("<!doctype html><title>Report</title><h1>Hello!</h1>");
```

### Rendering Quality

Layout and painting are done by AngleSharp.Renderer, which is still a young layout engine, while scripts run in AngleSharp.Js. Many sites work well, but do not expect the coverage of an established browser engine. See the [FAQ](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/tutorials/questions/index.html.md) for what to do when a page does not look right.


---

## Browser Engine (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/engine/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

The `BrowserEngine` represents a browsing context with its history, i.e., what a single browser window (or tab) would be. It is `IDisposable`; dispose it once the window goes away.

### Navigation

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NavigateAsync(address)` | Loads an address and adds it to the history. |
| `LoadHtmlAsync(html, address)` | Shows the given markup, optionally pretending it came from the given address. |
| `ReloadAsync()` | Loads the current address again. |
| `GoBackAsync()`, `GoForwardAsync()` | Moves through the history. |
| `GoAsync(delta)` | Jumps several entries back (negative) or forward. |
| `History` | A copy of the entries (address and title) and the index of the current one; `Back` and `Forward` list the entries before and after it, the closest first. |
| `Url`, `Title`, `IsLoading` | The state of the current page. |
| `CanGoBack`, `CanGoForward` | If there is something to go to. |

The address goes through `BrowserEngine.NormalizeAddress`, so what a user enters in an address bar works: `example.org` turns into `https://example.org`, while rooted paths of existing files turn into `file:` addresses. Addresses of the custom schemes of the engine (`BrowserOptions.SchemeHandlers`) stay as they are.

`Url` shows where the engine is going as soon as a navigation starts, like in any browser. A failed navigation does not throw: it raises `Error`, is recorded in the diagnostics, and shows an error page instead.

```cs
engine.StateChanged += (_, _) => Console.WriteLine($"{engine.Title} ({engine.Url}), loading: {engine.IsLoading}");

await engine.NavigateAsync("example.org");
Console.WriteLine(engine.CanGoBack);
```

### Site Information

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `IconUrls`, `IconUrl` | Where the page's icon may come from, best first: bitmaps of `<link rel="icon">`, then of `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">`, `/favicon.ico` of an HTTP(S) page, and declared SVG icons last. `IconUrl` is the first of them. |
| `LoadIconAsync()` | Loads the first of them that is an image, with the page's cookies and cache; `null` if there is none. Images are recognized by their content, as servers send icons with all kinds of content types. |
| `Certificate` | The `ServerCertificate` the server of the current HTTPS page presented. |
| `GetCertificate(host)` | The certificate a host presented the last time the engine connected to it. |

A changed icon raises `StateChanged`. A `ServerCertificate` is a snapshot of what the platform verified: names, issuer, validity, fingerprints, key, the chain up to the root, and `PolicyErrors` (`IsValid`). The engine captures it in the validation callback of its HTTP handler, keeping the platform's verdict; a host setting its own callback (via `BrowserOptions.ConfigureIo`) can use `ServerCertificate.Create` to the same end. A page served from the HTTP cache without a new connection may have no certificate.

```cs
engine.StateChanged += async (_, _) =>
{
    var icon = await engine.LoadIconAsync();
    Console.WriteLine($"{engine.IconUrl}: {icon?.Length ?? 0} bytes, issued by {engine.Certificate?.IssuerName}");
};
```

### Threading

AngleSharp is not thread-safe, so all DOM work is serialized and runs on AngleSharp's event loop. This has some consequences:

- All `*Async` methods of the engine may be called from any thread. They wait for the engine to be free.
- Code touching the DOM has to run in `InvokeAsync`, which also makes `Document` safe to use. Handlers of DOM events run on the event loop already.
- Engine events may be raised on any thread. A UI has to dispatch to its UI thread when handling them.
- Do not block the event loop (e.g., waiting for another engine operation in `InvokeAsync`): it would wait for itself.

```cs
var links = await engine.InvokeAsync(document => document?.QuerySelectorAll("a").Length ?? 0);
Console.WriteLine(links);
```

### Working With the DOM

`InvokeAsync` gets the current document, which is the regular AngleSharp DOM. CSS and script integration work as in AngleSharp.Css and AngleSharp.Js:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Dom;

await engine.InvokeAsync(document =>
{
    var heading = document?.QuerySelector("h1");

    if (heading is not null)
    {
        heading.TextContent = "Changed from .NET";
        heading.AddEventListener("click", (_, _) => Console.WriteLine("Clicked!"));
    }
});
```

Changing the DOM invalidates the page, i.e., hosts paint a new frame on their own.

The underlying `IBrowsingContext` is available via `Context`, e.g., to retrieve services.

### Events

| Event | Raised when |
| --- | --- |
| `Invalidated` | The visual output changed and a new frame should be painted. |
| `StateChanged` | The address, title, icon, loading state, or history state changed. |
| `HoverChanged` | The hovered link or the cursor changed. |
| `ScrollChanged` | The scroll position changed. |
| `WindowRequested` | The page asks for a new window. See [Configuration](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/configuration/index.html.md#multiple-windows). |
| `Error` | An operation failed, e.g., a navigation or a script. |

### Diagnostics

`Diagnostics` collects what happens while showing the current page, like the developer tools of a browser. It starts over with every page and is thread-safe:

```cs
await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

foreach (var request in engine.Diagnostics.Requests)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{request.Method} {request.Url}: {request.StatusCode} after {request.Duration}");
}

foreach (var message in engine.Diagnostics.Messages)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{message.Kind}] {message.ErrorType} {message.Text}");
    Console.WriteLine(message.StackTrace);
}

foreach (var frame in engine.Diagnostics.Frames)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{frame.Kind}: layout {frame.Layout} (styles {frame.Metrics.Style}), raster {frame.Raster}");
}
```

Requests come with their `StartedAt` and `Duration` as well as their `RequestHeaders` and `ResponseHeaders`. Errors tell as much as is known about them: `ErrorType`, `Line`, `Column` and the `StackTrace` of the script (or of the .NET exception, if no script threw). `Source` names the script, if known; AngleSharp.Js does not report that yet. `Frames` has the timings of the latest painted frames (those made by `PrepareFrameAsync` and rasterized), where `Kind` tells if the document was laid out (`Layout`), the last frame was patched (`Update`) or just moved (`Reposition`). The `Metrics` of a frame come from AngleSharp.Renderer and tell where the time of its layout went (`Setup`, `Style`, `Layout`, `HitTesting`, `Subframes`) and how much work that was (e.g., `Elements`, `Boxes`, `TrialLayouts`, `AllocatedBytes`); they are `RenderMetrics.None` for a frame that needed no layout.

The `Changed` event tells when there is something new. `Clear()` removes what has been collected so far.


---

## Rendering (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/rendering/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

There are two ways to get pixels out of the engine. Pick `PaintAsync` for occasional images, and frames for displaying a page continuously.

### Images

`PaintAsync` paints the current viewport into a PNG. It returns `null` if there is no document to paint yet:

```cs
engine.Resize(1024, 768);

var image = await engine.PaintAsync();

if (image is not null)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{image.Width}x{image.Height} {image.MimeType}");
    await File.WriteAllBytesAsync("page.png", image.Data);
}
```

### Frames

Encoding a PNG is too slow for showing a live page. Frames split the work into two steps instead, which allows a host to pipeline them:

1. `PrepareFrameAsync` lays out the page on the event loop. It returns `null` if no document is ready.
2. `BrowserFrame.Rasterize` turns the frame into raw premultiplied RGBA pixels. It does not touch the DOM, so it runs on any thread, while the engine already prepares the next frame.

```cs
var frame = await engine.PrepareFrameAsync();

if (frame is not null)
{
    var pixels = frame.Rasterize();
    Console.WriteLine($"{pixels.Width}x{pixels.Height}, {pixels.RowBytes} bytes per row, {pixels.Data.Length} in total");
}
```

Preparing a frame also refreshes what the engine knows for hit testing. The cursor and links are then looked up without touching the DOM, which keeps pointer moves responsive on busy pages.

Animated images (GIFs and WebPs of several frames) play on their own: when one in view shows its next frame, the engine raises `Invalidated`, and the next frame is the last one rasterized again, without a layout. An image plays from the moment it is first painted and as often as it tells, which is forever for most GIFs.

The first frame of a page shows up early: only what is in the viewport is styled and laid out for it. The engine asks for the next frame right away (it raises `Invalidated`), which lays out the whole page. Until then, the page below the viewport is blank, and the scroll position is not limited to the height of the page.

### Overscan and Scrolling

A frame may be larger than the viewport: `OverscanTop` rows are painted above the viewport, and some more below it. The viewport starts at row `OverscanTop`.

Scrolling is smooth and runs ahead of the DOM. Two properties reflect that:

- `ScrollPosition` is where the page should be right now, and changes without waiting for the event loop.
- `ScrollTop` is the scroll offset the DOM knows about.

Until the next frame arrives, a host displays the last frame shifted by the difference, which is what makes scrolling smooth even when layout takes a while:

```cs
var frame = await engine.PrepareFrameAsync();

if (frame is { IsScrollShiftable: true })
{
    var shift = frame.ScrollTop - engine.ScrollPosition;
    var y = shift - frame.OverscanTop;
    Console.WriteLine($"Draw the frame at {y}");
}
```

A frame of a page with fixed or sticky boxes cannot be shifted, which is what `IsScrollShiftable` tells.

`ScrollHeight` is the height of the page once measured, which allows drawing a scrollbar. Use `ScrollAsync` for relative changes (e.g., the mouse wheel) and `ScrollToAsync` for absolute ones (e.g., a scrollbar's thumb, with `animate: false`).

### Viewport and Color Scheme

`Resize` changes the size of the viewport in CSS pixels. Setting `ColorScheme` changes the answer to `prefers-color-scheme`. Both repaint the page.

```cs
engine.Resize(390, 844);
engine.ColorScheme = "dark";
```

The screen size reported to media queries is set via `BrowserOptions.ScreenWidth` and `BrowserOptions.ScreenHeight`.


---

## Input (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/input/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

The engine translates input into DOM interactions. It fires the same events as a browser, and performs the default actions of the page, such as following a link, focusing a text field, toggling a checkbox, or submitting a form.

All positions are in CSS pixels relative to the viewport.

### Pointer

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `MovePointer(x, y)` | Moves the pointer without waiting. Moves are coalesced, which is what a UI should use. |
| `MovePointerAsync(x, y)` | Moves the pointer and waits until the hover state has been updated. |
| `PointerDownAsync(x, y, modifiers)` | Presses the primary button. |
| `PointerDownAsync(x, y, clickCount, modifiers)` | Presses the primary button for the given time in a row, e.g., 2 for a double click. |
| `PointerUpAsync(x, y, modifiers)` | Releases the primary button. |
| `ClickAsync(x, y, modifiers)` | Presses and releases the primary button. |
| `HoveredLink`, `Cursor` | The link below the pointer and the `BrowserCursor` a host should display. |

Awaiting a click also awaits the navigation it caused:

```cs
await engine.ClickAsync(40, 390);
Console.WriteLine(engine.Url);
```

Holding Control while clicking a link requests a new window, as does a link with `target="_blank"`. See [Multiple Windows](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/configuration/index.html.md#multiple-windows).

```cs
await engine.ClickAsync(40, 390, InputModifiers.Control);
```

### Selecting Text

With `BrowserOptions.IsTextSelectionEnabled`, the text of a page can be selected as in a browser. It is off by default, as the layouts then also record where their text comes from.

- Pressing the button and moving the pointer with it held selects the text in between; with Shift, a press extends the selection.
- A second press in a row (`clickCount` 2) selects a word, a third one the paragraph.
- Control+A (or Cmd+A) selects all text of the page, unless a text field has the focus.
- Over text that can be selected, `Cursor` is `BrowserCursor.Text`, unless the page asks for another cursor.
- A page can cancel `mousedown` or `selectstart`, and `user-select: none` keeps text from being selected. Scripts see the selection through `getSelection()`.

`CopySelectionAsync` fires `copy` and returns the selected text for the clipboard, or an empty text if nothing is selected or the page canceled the event:

```cs
var engine = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions { IsTextSelectionEnabled = true });
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("<p>Hello world</p>");
await engine.PointerDownAsync(30, 20, 2);
await engine.PointerUpAsync(30, 20);
Console.WriteLine(await engine.CopySelectionAsync());
```

### Keyboard

Keys are named by their DOM key value, e.g., `"a"`, `"Enter"`, `"Backspace"`, `"Tab"`, or `"ArrowDown"`. Keys and text are separate on purpose, just like in most UI frameworks:

- `KeyDownAsync` and `KeyUpAsync` fire the keyboard events and perform the actions of keys, e.g., Tab moving the focus, or Enter submitting a form.
- `TextInputAsync` enters text into the focused text field. It works for whole strings, too.

```cs
await engine.ClickAsync(100, 200);
await engine.TextInputAsync("angle brackets");
await engine.KeyDownAsync("Enter");
await engine.KeyUpAsync("Enter");
```

### Selects

A `select` showing several options (`multiple` or `size`) is a list box:

- A click selects a row. With `multiple`, Ctrl (or Cmd) toggles it and Shift selects the rows from the last one clicked.
- The up and down keys move the selection, with Shift (and `multiple`) extending it.
- The wheel scrolls it before the page.

Any other `select` is a dropdown. Pressing it, or Enter, Space or Alt+Down while it has the focus, opens its list:

- `IsSelectPopupOpen` tells if the list is open. Frames from `PrepareFrameAsync` show it on top of the page (the image of `PaintAsync` does not), so a host has nothing to do for it. It stays within the viewport, opening above the select without room below.
- While it is open, the list takes all keys: they move its highlight (skipping what is disabled), Enter, Space or Tab choose the highlighted row, and Escape closes it without a change. A click on a row chooses it.
- A press elsewhere or scrolling the page closes it. So do the select losing the focus or going away, and a change of the viewport.
- While it is closed, the up and down keys, Home, End, Page Up, Page Down and typing change the value right away.
- The list uses the color scheme of the select: dark if its `color-scheme` (or else the `color-scheme` meta element of the page) supports dark, and doesn't also support light unless `ColorScheme` is `dark`. `ColorScheme` alone doesn't make it dark, as in other browsers. Colors of the select and of its options win over those of the scheme.

Choosing a row fires `input` and `change` if the value changed, then `click`.

### Scrolling

`ScrollAsync` scrolls by a distance: what is below the pointer, if that is a scroll container, or else the page. The returned task completes once the scrolling arrived.

```cs
await engine.MovePointerAsync(400, 300);
await engine.ScrollAsync(0, 480);
Console.WriteLine(engine.ScrollPosition);
```


---

## Configuration (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/configuration/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

Everything that touches the outside world is configured via `BrowserOptions`, which is passed to the constructor of the engine.

### Options

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ProfileDirectory` | `null` | Where cookies, web storage and the HTTP cache are persisted; `null` keeps everything in memory. |
| `UserAgent` | `null` | The user agent to report; `null` uses the default of AngleSharp.Io. |
| `DefaultHeaders` | empty | Headers added to every request, unless a request sets them already. |
| `ColorScheme` | `null` | The answer to `prefers-color-scheme`, e.g., `light` or `dark`. |
| `IsScriptingEnabled` | `true` | If JavaScript should be evaluated. |
| `ClipboardPlatform` | `null` | The clipboard exposed to pages; `null` means the API is not available. |
| `IsTextSelectionEnabled` | `false` | If the text of pages can be selected with the pointer and Control+A. |
| `ViewportWidth`, `ViewportHeight` | 1280, 800 | The initial viewport in CSS pixels. |
| `ScreenWidth`, `ScreenHeight` | 1920, 1080 | The screen size reported to media queries. |
| `FontSize` | 16 | The default font size in CSS pixels. |
| `ConfigureIo` | `null` | A callback customizing the IO options. |
| `Configure` | `null` | A callback extending the AngleSharp configuration. |
| `SchemeHandlers` | empty | Handlers answering the requests of custom URL schemes. |
| `AudioOutput` | `null` | Where the audio of pages plays; `null` plays it silently (`SilentAudioOutput`). |
| `AudioCodecs` | WAV, MP3, Ogg Vorbis, Ogg Opus | The audio formats that play, in the order they are tried. |
| `IsAutoplayAllowed` | `false` | If pages may play audible media before the user pressed or typed something. |

```cs
var options = new BrowserOptions
{
    ProfileDirectory = "profile",
    UserAgent = "MyApp/1.0",
    ColorScheme = "dark",
    ViewportWidth = 1024,
    ViewportHeight = 768,
};

options.DefaultHeaders["Accept-Language"] = "de";

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(options);
```

### Profiles

Without a `ProfileDirectory` nothing survives the engine, which is what you want for tests and automation. With one, a later engine using the same directory finds its cookies, storage and cache again.

### Customizing IO and AngleSharp

`ConfigureIo` runs after the defaults have been derived from the other options. It gives access to all of `IoOptions` from AngleSharp.Io, e.g., the HTTP handler:

```cs
using System.Net;

var options = new BrowserOptions
{
    ConfigureIo = io => io.HttpHandler.Proxy = new WebProxy("http://localhost:8080"),
};
```

Like a browser, the handler decompresses responses (gzip, deflate and brotli; `AutomaticDecompression`), which some servers send even if not asked to.

Pages can register service workers (`navigator.serviceWorker`, through `ServiceWorkerPlatform`). The workers are installed and activated, but their scripts don't run, so every request goes to the network. Setting `io.ServiceWorkerPlatform` to `null` in `ConfigureIo` removes the API, and another platform can run the workers.

`Configure` receives the AngleSharp configuration before the browsing context is created, so further services can be added:

```cs
using AngleSharp;

var options = new BrowserOptions
{
    Configure = config => config.WithLocaleBasedEncoding(),
};
```

### Custom Schemes

`SchemeHandlers` registers URL schemes of the host, e.g., for its own pages. A handler gets the request and answers a response, or `null` if there is nothing at the address. Pages can link to these addresses, and `NavigateAsync` keeps them as they are (`Schemes` lists them; `BrowserEngine.NormalizeAddress(address, schemes)` does the same for an address bar):

```cs
using System.IO;
using System.Net;
using System.Text;
using AngleSharp.Io;

var options = new BrowserOptions();
options.SchemeHandlers["app"] = (request, cancellationToken) =>
{
    var response = new DefaultResponse
    {
        Address = request.Address,
        StatusCode = HttpStatusCode.OK,
        Content = new MemoryStream(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes($"<h1>{request.Address.Data}</h1>")),
    };
    response.Headers[HeaderNames.ContentType] = "text/html; charset=utf-8";
    return Task.FromResult<IResponse?>(response);
};

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(options);
await engine.NavigateAsync("app:settings");
```

The handlers are asked before the built-in requesters, so a handler for `http` would take over the network.

### Audio

Pages play audio with `audio` elements and `new Audio(src)`, including `play()` (a promise), `pause()`, `currentTime`, `volume`, `muted`, `loop`, `autoplay` and their events (`playing`, `timeupdate`, `ended`, ...). The formats of `AudioCodecs` are decoded with managed code only: WAV (PCM or floats), MP3 (NLayer), Ogg Vorbis (NVorbis) and Ogg Opus (Concentus). Other formats (e.g. AAC in MP4) answer an empty `canPlayType`, so pages offering several `source` elements get one that plays, and fail with an `error` (`MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED`) otherwise. The engine reads the whole file before it plays.

Where the audio is heard is up to the host, as it depends on the platform. An `IAudioOutput` opens a stream per media element playing, which pulls the samples (32-bit floats, the channels interleaved) as it plays them; the media's clock advances with what was pulled:

```cs
sealed class DeviceOutput : IAudioOutput
{
    public IAudioStream Open(AudioFormat format, IAudioSource source) =>
        new DeviceStream(format, source); // e.g. an OpenAL source fed from source.Read
}

var options = new BrowserOptions
{
    AudioOutput = new DeviceOutput(),
};
```

Vision plays on the default device via OpenAL Soft (`src/Vision/Audio/OpenAlAudioOutput.cs`, using Silk.NET.OpenAL), which can serve as a starting point. Without an output, the media plays silently in real time, with its events and its end, which is what tests and automation want. Like browsers, audible media only plays once the user pressed or typed something on the page (`play()` rejects with a `NotAllowedError` before); muted media always plays, and `IsAutoplayAllowed` lifts the rule. Media stops once its document is left.

An `audio` element with the `controls` attribute shows the controls of Chrome (300x54 by default): a play/pause button, the time, a timeline and a mute button. A press on them plays, pauses, mutes or seeks (also while the timeline is dragged); the hit testing is AngleSharp.Renderer's `GetMediaControlAt` and `GetMediaTimelinePosition`. While media plays, the time and the timeline go on in the last frame (rasterized again, like the frames of a GIF) without a layout; only playing, pausing, seeking or a change of the volume lays the page out. One without `controls` is not rendered.

### Multiple Windows

One engine stands for one window. When a page asks for another window (a link with `target="_blank"`, or a link clicked with Control), the engine raises `WindowRequested`. If the request is not marked as handled the page navigates in place, so there is nothing to do if a host only has a single window.

`CreateWindow` creates the engine of another window. It has its own browsing context and history, but shares the profile (cookies, storage, caches), even without a profile directory:

```cs
engine.WindowRequested += (_, request) =>
{
    // must be set while handling the event, which is raised on the engine's thread
    request.Handled = true;

    _ = Task.Run(async () =>
    {
        var window = engine.CreateWindow();
        await window.NavigateAsync(request.Url);
    });
};
```

The caller owns the returned engine and has to dispose it. An overload takes other options for the new window, e.g., after settings changed.


---

## Avalonia Control (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/avalonia/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

The `AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia` package provides `BrowserView`, a control displaying a web page. It has no native browser dependency: pages are parsed, scripted and painted in .NET. The control paints frames, forwards pointer, wheel and keyboard input, draws an overlay scrollbar, and shows the cursor the page asks for.

The package relies on `Avalonia` only, so the application decides on the theme and platform packages. Rendering pages does not require a specific Avalonia renderer.

### The Simple Way

Set the `Source`:

```xml
<Window xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
        xmlns:browser="using:AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia">
    <browser:BrowserView Source="https://example.org" />
</Window>
```

The control creates an engine while it is in the visual tree, and disposes it when it gets detached. Nothing is persisted. The clipboard of the window is connected, and pages are told the color scheme of the current theme, following it when it changes.

`Source` is what navigates: setting it opens another page. It also follows the page, e.g., after a click on a link. By default it binds two-way, which is all it takes for an address bar. Note the update trigger, as otherwise every keystroke would navigate:

```xml
<DockPanel xmlns="https://github.com/avaloniaui"
           xmlns:x="http://schemas.microsoft.com/winfx/2006/xaml"
           xmlns:browser="using:AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia">
    <TextBox DockPanel.Dock="Top" Text="{Binding #View.Source, UpdateSourceTrigger=LostFocus}" />
    <browser:BrowserView x:Name="View" Source="https://example.org" />
</DockPanel>
```

The `Options` property configures the engine created by the control. Set it before the view is attached:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;
using AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia;

var view = new BrowserView
{
    Source = "https://example.org",
    Options = new BrowserOptions
    {
        ProfileDirectory = "profile",
        IsScriptingEnabled = false,
    },
};
```

The created engine is available from the `Engine` property, once the view is attached.

### Providing the Engine

Host the engine yourself to go beyond a page in a box: to reuse it after the view was detached, to control its lifetime, or to bind against it in a view model.

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;
using AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia;

var engine = new BrowserEngine();
var view = new BrowserView { Engine = engine };

await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");
```

An engine provided like this belongs to you: the control never disposes it, and `Options` does not apply to it. To allow pages to access the clipboard, set `BrowserOptions.ClipboardPlatform` to an `AvaloniaClipboardPlatform` with the clipboard of the top level.

If the assigned engine shows a page already, `Source` is updated with its address. Otherwise, the engine opens the `Source`, if there is any.

### Toolbar and Windows

The control has no chrome. The engine has what it takes for building one:

```cs
using Avalonia.Threading;

engine.StateChanged += (_, _) => Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() =>
{
    // update the title, back / forward buttons, or a progress indicator
    Console.WriteLine($"{engine.Title} ({engine.Url}), loading: {engine.IsLoading}");
});

engine.HoverChanged += (_, _) => Dispatcher.UIThread.Post(() =>
{
    // show the link's address in a status bar
    Console.WriteLine(engine.HoveredLink);
});
```

Engine events may be raised on any thread, so they are dispatched here. To open real windows for `target="_blank"` links, handle `WindowRequested`; see [Multiple Windows](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/configuration/index.html.md#multiple-windows).

### Input Handling

The control has to be focused to get keyboard input; clicking it does that. Shortcuts with Control or Alt stay unhandled, so `KeyBinding`s of the window work while the page is focused. Control+V pastes into the focused text field, Control+C copies the selected text and Control+A selects all of it (with `BrowserOptions.IsTextSelectionEnabled`), and the extra mouse buttons go back and forward in the history.

### Namespace Hint

Inside of a namespace below `AngleSharp.Browser`, the name `Avalonia` refers to `AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia`. Should your code live in one, put the `using` directives for Avalonia outside of the namespace, or write `global::Avalonia`.


---

## Vision Sample (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/vision/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

Vision is the sample application living in `src/Vision`: a small desktop browser built on `AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia`. It is a proof of concept, which shows how the packages fit together, and is not shipped as a package.

### Running

```sh
dotnet run --project src/Vision -- https://example.org
```

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `<address>` | The address to open instead of the start page. |
| `--profile <directory>` | The directory to use for cookies, web storage and the HTTP cache. |
| `--in-memory` | Persists no browsing data. |

New windows open `vision:start` unless the settings say otherwise: the pages visited most, a few demos and Vision's own pages. All of Vision's pages are listed at `vision:pages`; `vision:requester` sends HTTP requests with the requesters of the window (with its user agent, default headers and cookies) and shows the responses. Requests can be saved there under a name (the button below the response asks for it), and are kept with the profile (`requests.json`); the menu button in the top-left corner opens a sheet with the saved ones.

The profile and the settings are kept in the `Vision` folder of the local application data directory by default.

### What to Look At

| File | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| `App.axaml.cs` | One engine per window, sharing a profile using `CreateWindow`, and handling `WindowRequested`. |
| `ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs` | A toolbar and status bar on top of the engine's state and events, including the page's icon. |
| `Views/MainWindow.axaml` | Placing `BrowserView` in a window, next to a second one for the diagnostics. |
| `Models/BrowserSettings.cs` | Turning user settings into `BrowserOptions`. |
| `Audio/OpenAlAudioOutput.cs` | An `IAudioOutput` playing the audio of pages on the default device (OpenAL Soft via Silk.NET), shared by all windows, silent without a device. |
| `Pages/` | The app's own UI (start page, requester, diagnostics, inspector, settings, site information, about) written as HTML and CSS, and wired up with .NET event handlers through `InvokeAsync`, in an engine with scripting disabled. Their text can be selected and copied like the one of pages. |


---

## API Documentation (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/tutorials/api/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

### Quick API Map

The following APIs cover most day-to-day tasks:

- `new BrowserEngine(options)`
: Creates a browsing context with a history; dispose it when done.
- `NavigateAsync`, `LoadHtmlAsync`, `ReloadAsync`, `GoBackAsync`, `GoForwardAsync`, `GoAsync`
: Changes what is shown.
- `InvokeAsync`, `EvaluateScriptAsync`
: Runs .NET code against the DOM, or JavaScript in the page.
- `PaintAsync`
: Paints the viewport into a PNG.
- `PrepareFrameAsync`, `BrowserFrame.Rasterize`
: Paints raw frames for displaying a live page.
- `ClickAsync`, `TextInputAsync`, `KeyDownAsync`, `ScrollAsync`
: Interacts with the page like a user.
- `Diagnostics`
: Lists the requests, errors, console output and frame timings of the page.
- `BrowserView`
: Displays an engine in Avalonia.

### BrowserEngine

#### State

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Url`, `Title` | The address (including one being loaded) and the title. |
| `IsLoading` | If a navigation is ongoing. |
| `IconUrl`, `IconUrls`, `Certificate` | The page's icon and the `ServerCertificate` of its connection. See [Site Information](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/engine/index.html.md#site-information). |
| `CanGoBack`, `CanGoForward` | The state of the history. |
| `Document`, `Context` | The current `IDocument` (use it within `InvokeAsync`) and the `IBrowsingContext`. |
| `ViewportWidth`, `ViewportHeight` | The size of the viewport in CSS pixels. |
| `ScrollPosition`, `ScrollTop`, `ScrollHeight` | The target of the smooth scrolling, the DOM's offset, and the page's height. |
| `HoveredLink`, `Cursor` | What is below the pointer. |
| `ColorScheme` | The answer to `prefers-color-scheme`; may be changed. |
| `HasPaintedDocument` | If the current document has been painted at least once. |
| `Diagnostics` | The `BrowserDiagnostics` of the current page. |

#### Methods

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `NormalizeAddress(address)` | Turns the input of an address bar into an absolute address (static). |
| `NavigateAsync(address)` | Loads an address. |
| `LoadHtmlAsync(html, address)` | Shows the given source code. |
| `ReloadAsync()`, `GoBackAsync()`, `GoForwardAsync()`, `GoAsync(delta)` | Moves in the history. |
| `History` | A copy of the history's entries (address and title) and the index of the current one. |
| `Resize(width, height)` | Changes the viewport. |
| `PaintAsync()` | Returns a `RenderedImage` with a PNG, or `null`. |
| `PrepareFrameAsync()` | Returns a `BrowserFrame`, or `null`. |
| `EvaluateScriptAsync(script)` | Runs a script, and returns its completion value. |
| `InvokeAsync(action)` | Runs code on the event loop, and returns its value. |
| `MovePointer`, `MovePointerAsync`, `PointerDownAsync`, `PointerUpAsync`, `ClickAsync` | Pointer input. |
| `KeyDownAsync`, `KeyUpAsync`, `TextInputAsync` | Keyboard input. |
| `CopySelectionAsync()` | Gets the selected text for the clipboard. |
| `ScrollAsync(deltaX, deltaY)`, `ScrollToAsync(top, animate)` | Scrolling. |
| `CreateWindow()`, `CreateWindow(options)` | Creates an engine sharing the profile. |
| `LoadIconAsync()`, `GetCertificate(host)` | Loads the page's icon, or gets the certificate of a host. |

All asynchronous methods take an optional `CancellationToken`.

#### Events

`Invalidated`, `StateChanged`, `HoverChanged`, `ScrollChanged`, `WindowRequested`, and `Error`. See [Browser Engine](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/engine/index.html.md#events).

### BrowserFrame

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Width`, `Height` | The size in CSS pixels, including the overscan. |
| `OverscanTop` | The rows above the viewport. |
| `ScrollTop` | The scroll offset it was painted at. |
| `IsScrollShiftable` | If it may be shifted to show another offset. |
| `Rasterize()` | Returns the `RenderedPixels` (premultiplied RGBA); safe from any thread. |

### BrowserDiagnostics

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Requests` | A list of `NetworkEntry`: `Method`, `Url`, `StartedAt`, `Duration`, `StatusCode`, `ContentType`, `ContentLength`, `RequestHeaders`, `ResponseHeaders`, `IsPending`. |
| `Messages` | A list of `DiagnosticMessage`: `Kind` (`Console` or `Error`), `Time`, `Text`, and for errors `ErrorType`, `Source`, `Line`, `Column`, `StackTrace`. |
| `Frames` | A list of `FrameTiming` for the latest painted frames: `Time`, `Kind` (`Layout`, `Update` or `Reposition`), `Layout`, `Raster`, and the `Metrics` of the renderer (the time of each phase and how much work it did). |
| `Changed` | Raised when something was added or cleared, on any thread. |
| `Clear()` | Removes what has been collected. |

### BrowserView

| Member | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Source` | The address of the page; a styled property binding two-way by default. |
| `Engine` | The displayed engine; a styled property. |
| `Options` | The options for the engine created by the view. |

`AvaloniaClipboardPlatform` connects an Avalonia clipboard to `BrowserOptions.ClipboardPlatform`.

The options are described in [Configuration](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/configuration/index.html.md).


---

## Examples (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/tutorials/examples/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

This page shows some recipes for working with AngleSharp.Browser.

### Take a Screenshot

```cs
using System.IO;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions { ViewportWidth = 1280, ViewportHeight = 800 });

await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

var image = await engine.PaintAsync();
await File.WriteAllBytesAsync("example.png", image!.Data);
```

### Compare a Page in Light and Dark

```cs
using System.IO;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("""
    <!doctype html>
    <style>
      body { background: white; color: black; }
      @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background: black; color: white; } }
    </style>
    <h1>Hello</h1>
    """);

foreach (var scheme in new[] { "light", "dark" })
{
    engine.ColorScheme = scheme;
    var image = await engine.PaintAsync();
    await File.WriteAllBytesAsync($"{scheme}.png", image!.Data);
}
```

### Type Into a Form Field

Clicking the field focuses it, and the text arrives as input events:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("""
    <!doctype html>
    <input id="name">
    <p id="out"></p>
    <script>
      document.getElementById('name').addEventListener('input', function (ev) {
        document.getElementById('out').textContent = 'Hello ' + ev.target.value;
      });
    </script>
    """);

await engine.PaintAsync();
await engine.ClickAsync(50, 18);
await engine.TextInputAsync("Vision");

var text = await engine.InvokeAsync(document => document?.GetElementById("out")?.TextContent);
Console.WriteLine(text);
```

### Follow a Link

Awaiting the click covers the navigation it started:

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("""<!doctype html><body style="margin:0"><a href="data:text/html,%3Ctitle%3ENext%3C/title%3E">Go on</a>""");

await engine.PaintAsync();
await engine.ClickAsync(10, 8);

Console.WriteLine(engine.Title);
await engine.GoBackAsync();
Console.WriteLine(engine.CanGoForward);
```

### Find Slow or Failed Requests

```cs
using System.Linq;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();
await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

var problems = engine.Diagnostics.Requests.Where(m => m.Duration > TimeSpan.FromSeconds(1) || (int?)m.StatusCode >= 400);

foreach (var request in problems)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{request.StatusCode} {request.Url} ({request.Duration})");
}
```

### Read the Console of a Page

```cs
using System.Linq;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("<!doctype html><script>console.log('Hello from the page');</script>");

foreach (var message in engine.Diagnostics.Messages.Where(m => m.Kind == DiagnosticKind.Console))
{
    Console.WriteLine(message.Text);
}
```

### Disable Scripts

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions { IsScriptingEnabled = false });
await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

var title = await engine.InvokeAsync(document => document?.Title);
Console.WriteLine(title);
```

### HTML as Your Own UI

Vision writes its settings and about windows like this: no JavaScript, with the logic in C#.

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;
using AngleSharp.Dom;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions { IsScriptingEnabled = false });
await engine.LoadHtmlAsync("""<!doctype html><body style="margin:0"><button id="save" style="width:100px;height:40px">Save</button>""");

await engine.InvokeAsync(document =>
{
    document?.GetElementById("save")?.AddEventListener("click", (_, _) => Console.WriteLine("Saved!"));
});

await engine.PaintAsync();
await engine.ClickAsync(20, 20);
```


---

## Writing a Custom Host (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/tutorials/custom-host/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

The engine knows nothing about a UI, so it can be displayed in any framework. This tutorial walks through what `BrowserView` does for Avalonia. Its source in `src/AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia/BrowserView.cs` is the complete reference.

### 1. Connect the Engine

Listen to the events of the engine, and tell it about the size of the view. Keep in mind that events may be raised on any thread.

```cs
using AngleSharp.Browser;

using var engine = new BrowserEngine();

engine.Invalidated += (_, _) => { /* schedule painting */ };
engine.ScrollChanged += (_, _) => { /* redraw the last frame on the UI thread */ };
engine.HoverChanged += (_, _) => { /* update the cursor from engine.Cursor on the UI thread */ };

engine.Resize(800, 600);
```

### 2. Paint in a Loop

`Invalidated` may be raised much more often than a UI displays frames. Requests are coalesced into a dirty flag, and a single loop paints while there are changes. Layout and raster overlap, which keeps a higher frame rate than doing them one after the other:

```cs
using System.Threading;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using AngleSharp.Browser;

var dirty = 1;
Task? presenting = null;

while (Interlocked.Exchange(ref dirty, 0) == 1)
{
    var frame = await engine.PrepareFrameAsync();

    if (presenting is not null)
    {
        await presenting;
    }

    presenting = frame is null ? null : Task.Run(() =>
    {
        var pixels = frame.Rasterize();
        // copy pixels.Data to a bitmap; rows are pixels.RowBytes long and in premultiplied RGBA
        // then, on the UI thread, make the bitmap and the frame's scroll information current
        return pixels.Width;
    });
}

if (presenting is not null)
{
    await presenting;
}
```

A loop like this should be limited to about 60 frames per second, and restarted when `Invalidated` is raised. Catch `ObjectDisposedException` to end it with the engine.

### 3. Draw the Frame

When drawing, shift the frame to the current scroll position, and leave out the overscan. The values to remember from the frame are `ScrollTop`, `OverscanTop` and `IsScrollShiftable`:

```cs
var frame = await engine.PrepareFrameAsync();

if (frame is not null)
{
    var shift = frame.IsScrollShiftable ? frame.ScrollTop - engine.ScrollPosition : 0;
    var top = shift - frame.OverscanTop;
    // draw the bitmap at (0, top), clipped to the view
    Console.WriteLine(top);
}
```

Clear with white first, as the frame only covers the page once there is a document.

### 4. Forward the Input

Translate the events of the framework. All of these are fire-and-forget from the perspective of the UI, but observe the tasks to log exceptions:

| UI event | Engine call |
| --- | --- |
| Pointer moved | `MovePointer(x, y)` |
| Primary button pressed / released | `PointerDownAsync` (with the click count, for selecting words) / `PointerUpAsync` |
| Back / forward button pressed | `GoBackAsync` / `GoForwardAsync` |
| Back / forward button held (its menu) | `History.Back` / `History.Forward`, then `GoAsync(delta)` for the entry chosen |
| Wheel | `ScrollAsync(-deltaX * distance, -deltaY * distance)` |
| Key pressed / released | `KeyDownAsync` / `KeyUpAsync`, with the DOM's name of the key |
| Text entered | `TextInputAsync` |

`MovePointer` looks up the cursor and hovered link in the last frame right away, and coalesces the DOM events, so a busy page does not make the pointer lag.

### 5. Offer the Rest

What else makes it feel like a browser:

- Set `BrowserOptions.ClipboardPlatform` with an implementation of `IClipboardPlatform` from AngleSharp.Io.
- Set `BrowserOptions.IsTextSelectionEnabled`, and put the text of `CopySelectionAsync` on the clipboard for Control+C.
- Update `ColorScheme` when the theme changes.
- Draw a scrollbar from `ScrollPosition`, `ScrollHeight` and `ViewportHeight`, and change the position using `ScrollToAsync`.
- Handle `WindowRequested`, and open a window with an engine from `CreateWindow`.


---

## Questions (AngleSharp.Browser)

> Source: https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/tutorials/questions/
> Project: AngleSharp.Browser (https://github.com/AngleSharp/AngleSharp.Browser)
> Package: AngleSharp.Browser 0.2.0 — install with `dotnet add package AngleSharp.Browser`
> Docs revision: 9e2ca98df15342044069b89c6ba35431334e1443

### A page looks wrong or stays empty. What can I do?

Look at the diagnostics first, as many issues come from a script that failed, or a resource not being loaded:

```cs
foreach (var message in engine.Diagnostics.Messages)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"[{message.Kind}] {message.Text}");
}
```

Layout and painting are done by AngleSharp.Renderer, styles by AngleSharp.Css, and scripts by AngleSharp.Js. Sites relying on the page being rendered by a client-side framework are the most likely to stay empty, as a single unsupported API may stop their script. Please open an issue in the respective repository with a small reproduction.

### How do I wait until a page is ready?

The task returned by `NavigateAsync` completes once the document has been loaded. Scripts may keep on changing the page afterwards. There is no general answer for when such a page is finished, so wait for what you are looking for:

```cs
await engine.NavigateAsync("https://example.org");

while (await engine.InvokeAsync(document => document?.QuerySelector("p")) is null)
{
    await Task.Delay(100);
}
```

### Why does my code throw or behave strangely when using the document?

AngleSharp is not thread-safe, so the DOM must only be used on the event loop. Use `InvokeAsync`. Do not keep elements around to use them outside of it. See [Threading](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/engine/index.html.md#threading).

### Why does waiting for the engine hang in my code?

The event loop is waiting for itself if an operation of the engine is awaited with blocking inside of `InvokeAsync` or a DOM event handler. Start the operation outside, instead.

Prefer `await` over `Wait()` and `Result` in general. This includes tests: assertions that block while running async code (e.g., `Assert.ThrowsAsync` of NUnit) may hang, so use an awaited `try` / `catch` instead.

### Why do `ScrollPosition` and `ScrollTop` differ?

Scrolling is smooth and runs ahead of the DOM. See [Overscan and Scrolling](https://anglesharp.github.io/docs/browser/general/rendering/index.html.md#overscan-and-scrolling).

### How do I persist logins?

Use a `ProfileDirectory`. Without one, cookies and storage are gone with the engine:

```cs
using var persistent = new BrowserEngine(new BrowserOptions { ProfileDirectory = "profile" });
```

### Why does a `data:` address show an empty page?

Characters like `<` need to be percent-encoded in the address. Use `Uri.EscapeDataString`, or `LoadHtmlAsync` to show markup:

```cs
await engine.NavigateAsync("data:text/html," + Uri.EscapeDataString("<title>Hello</title>"));
```

### Does the engine run on servers without a display?

Yes. Painting only requires SkiaSharp, whose native assets are included. On Linux they depend on fontconfig, so make sure it and some fonts are installed. Only `AngleSharp.Browser.Avalonia` needs a UI.

### How do I make large pages paint faster?

Use the server GC in the application. Laying out a large page keeps a lot alive until it is done (the styles and boxes of all elements), which the default workstation GC copies on a single thread for every collection meanwhile; the server GC does it on all cores, and its heaps adapt to the size of the application. For GitHub's start page, the pauses for garbage collection went from about 150 ms to 40 ms per frame, for about 200 MB more memory:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <ServerGarbageCollection>true</ServerGarbageCollection>
</PropertyGroup>
```

The first frames of a page are mostly spent compiling and optimizing code. A host shortens them by publishing precompiled code, and by not having the runtime wait for a quiet moment before it optimizes what is called often:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <PublishReadyToRun Condition="'$(RuntimeIdentifier)' != ''">true</PublishReadyToRun>
</PropertyGroup>

<ItemGroup>
  <RuntimeHostConfigurationOption Include="System.Runtime.TieredCompilation.CallCountingDelayMs" Value="0" />
</ItemGroup>
```

The styles and the style maps of large pages are computed on all cores. A host that has none to spare turns this off with the AppContext switches `AngleSharp.Css.DisableParallelism` and `AngleSharp.Renderer.DisableParallelism`.
